basis: Microcephaly and limb abnormalities define the syndrome; developmental delay/intellectual disability occurs in 15/29.
Inflammation of the iris and ciliary body, predominantly immune-mediated or infectious; systemic organ damage is not intrinsic.
Subtype of primary biliary cholangitis, an autoimmune disease damaging intrahepatic bile ducts.
Defined by transient thyroid hormone deficiency in infancy; no common direct extra-endocrine damage established.
Tumor originates in breast tissue, which has no axis; malignant transformation and metastases are uncommon.
Rod-cone dystrophy and sensorineural hearing loss define Usher syndrome; vestibular dysfunction shares the otologic axis.
Mature T-cell lymphoma; no additional organ has established common direct damage here. Rash alone does not establish cutaneous infiltration.
Mitochondrial myopathy causes ophthalmoplegia; developmental delay reported in 20/20 supports neurologic involvement. Cardiac and hearing findings are occasional.
Inherited dental enamel formation defect; amelogenesis imperfecta and enamel hypoplasia occur in 4/4.
Neutropenia with lymphocyte deficiency; stomatitis 3/3 and gingivitis 2/3 support oral damage; intellectual disability 2/3. Separately diagnosed infections excluded.
Inherited coagulation defect with recurrent thromboembolism; osteonecrosis parentage alone does not establish common skeletal damage.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing impairment reported in 9/9.
Predominant origins are oral cavity/salivary glands and pharyngeal/laryngeal airways; rarer eye, ear and endocrine subtypes do not define the umbrella.
Structural disorder of the iris pigment layer; no extraocular involvement established.
Failure of bone marrow blood-cell production defines the group; syndromic extra-organ findings vary among subtypes.
Bilateral congenital fusion of the humerus and radius.
Skeletal muscle degeneration, weakness and contractures define the umbrella; brain and eye abnormalities are subtype-dependent.
Cleft palate, ocular colobomata and radial synostosis define the syndrome; deafness is also a major defining feature, supporting otologic involvement.
Schwann-cell nerve sheath tumor, usually involving spinal nerve roots; pigmentation does not imply skin origin.
Molecular subtype of a central nervous system atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor; melanosomal gene expression does not establish skin disease.
Growth restriction with characteristic skeletal abnormalities; dental enamel defects occur frequently (30-79%), supporting gastrointestinal involvement.
Cardiomyopathy 2/5; myopathy/weakness and encephalopathy 80-99%. Common hepatic involvement, supported by hepatomegaly/transaminitis, omitted at the four-axis cap.
Localized lymph collection; lymphatic spaces are outside the specified axes, and damage to a listed organ is not intrinsic.
Complex congenital cardiac defects predominate. Asplenia 4/14 (~29%) is below threshold; abnormal visceral position alone does not establish organ damage.
Congenital accessory nostril affects the nasal airway; specific associated eye and other structural abnormalities are uncommon.
